Proposition 3.7, page 48 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((B_n)_{n\ge0}\) be the Markov chain on \(\{0,1\}\) with \(\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1\) and \(\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12\), let \(x_0>0\), and put \(x_{n+1}=3x_n\) if \(B_n=1\) and \(x_{n+1}=x_n/2\) if \(B_n=0\), with \(\mathcal{F}_n=\sigma(B_0,\ldots,B_n)\) (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map, which sends an even \(m\) to \(m/2\) and an odd \(m\) to \(3m+1\), where \(B_n\) models the parity of the \(n\)th iterate). Write \(\delta^{*}=\log(\sqrt3/2)\). Then (i) the stationary law of the chain satisfies \(\mathbb{P}(B_n=1)=\tfrac13\), and the fraction of odd steps (indices \(i\) with \(B_i=1\)) among the first \(n\) steps converges to \(\tfrac13\) almost surely from any initial state; (ii) \((x_n)\) is not a martingale, since \(\mathbb{E}[x_{n+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_n]=3x_n\) on \(\{B_n=1\}\), but \(M_n=3^{B_n}x_n\) is a martingale; (iii) \((\log x_n)\) is not a supermartingale, since its increment is \(+\log3\) on \(\{B_n=1\}\), but \(\log M_n\) is a supermartingale with conditional drift \(0\) on \(\{B_n=1\}\) and \(\delta^{*}\) on \(\{B_n=0\}\); (iv) almost surely \(\frac1n\log x_n\to\tfrac13\log3 - \tfrac23\log2=\tfrac13\log\tfrac34=\tfrac23\delta^{*}\approx -0.0959\); (v) if \(\tau_1<\tau_2<\cdots\) are the successive times at which \(B_n=1\), then \(X_j=x_{\tau_j}\) satisfies \(X_{j+1}=3X_j2^{-K_{j+1}}\), where \(K_{j+1}=\tau_{j+1} - \tau_j - 1\) are independent with the Geometric\((\tfrac12)\) law \(\mathbb{P}(K=k)=2^{-k}\) for \(k\ge1\), and \((X_j)\) is a martingale because \(\mathbb{E}[3\cdot2^{-K}]=3\sum_{k\ge1}4^{-k}=1\).
Source: book/chapters/ch03_stochastic.tex, label prop:ch3:standard.




Proposition 3.12, page 56 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((B_n)_{n\ge0}\) be the Markov chain on \(\{0,1\}\) with \(\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1\) and \(\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12\) (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map, where \(B_n\) models the parity of the \(n\)th iterate), started from its stationary law. Then \((B_n)\) is stationary with \(\mathbb{P}(B_n=1)=\frac{1}{1+\mathbb{E}[K]}=\frac13\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(B_n)=\frac29\), where \(K\), the number of zeros between successive ones of the chain, has the Geometric\((\tfrac12)\) law \(\mathbb{P}(K=k)=2^{-k}\) for \(k\ge1\) (so \(\mathbb{E}[K]=2\)), and its autocorrelation function is \(\rho(h)=\operatorname{Corr}(B_n,B_{n+h})=\bigl(-\tfrac12\bigr)^{h}\) for \(h\ge0\).
Source: book/chapters/ch03_stochastic.tex, label thm:autocorr.




Corollary 3.14, page 58 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \((B_n)_{n\ge0}\) be the Markov chain on \(\{0,1\}\) with \(\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1\) and \(\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12\), started from any initial state, let \(x_0>0\), and put \(x_{n+1}=3x_n\) if \(B_n=1\) and \(x_{n+1}=x_n/2\) if \(B_n=0\) (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map). Let \(\rho(h)=(-\tfrac12)^h\) be the autocorrelation function of \((B_n)\). The autocorrelation factor is \(\mathcal{A}:=1+2\sum_{h\ge1}\rho(h)=1+2\cdot\frac{-1/2}{1+1/2}=\frac13\), and the variance of the log path satisfies \(\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\log x_n)}{n}\longrightarrow\mathcal{A}\cdot\frac29(\log6)^2=\frac{2}{27}(\log6)^2\approx0.2378\) as \(n\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch03_stochastic.tex, label cor:longrun.




Proposition 3.17, page 61 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(x_0>1\) and let \(\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots\) be independent random variables with \(\mathbb{P}(\xi_i=\tfrac12)=\mathbb{P}(\xi_i=\tfrac32)=\tfrac12\), and put \(x_n=x_0\xi_1\cdots\xi_n\) (the Bernoulli model for the accelerated Collatz map) and \(\tau=\inf\{n\ge0:x_n\le1\}\). Then \(\tau<\infty\) almost surely, the stopped process \((x_{n\wedge\tau})_{n\ge0}\) is a nonnegative martingale converging almost surely to \(x_\tau\le1\), and it is not uniformly integrable. More precisely, for every \(n\), \(\mathbb{E}\bigl[x_n\mathbf{1}_{\{\tau>n\}}\bigr]\ge x_0 - 1\), while \(\mathbb{P}(\tau>n)\to0\) as \(n\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch03_stochastic.tex, label prop:uimartingale.

title: Results by chapter On the Collatz Conjecture
text:
Proposition 4.5, page 70 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider the stride model of the Collatz map. Let \(K_1,K_2,\dots\) be independent random variables with \(\mathbb{P}(K_j=k)=2^{-k}\) for \(k\ge1\) (the Geometric\((\tfrac12)\) law), fix \(x_0>1\), and put \(x_j=x_{j-1}\cdot3\cdot2^{-K_j}\), so that \(\log x_j=\log x_0+\Delta_1+\dots+\Delta_j\) with \(\Delta_j=\log3-K_j\log2\). Let \(\tau\) be the first \(j\) with \(\log x_j\le0\), and let \(O=-\log x_\tau\ge0\) be the overshoot below \(0\) at time \(\tau\). Then \(\log2\le\mathbb{E}[O]<2\log2\) and [_{x_0}[]<.]
Source: book/chapters/ch04_lyapunov.tex, label prop:ch4:passage.




Theorem 4.7, page 71 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(S\) be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, \(S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{k}\) with \(k=v_2(3x+1)\), where \(v_2(m)\) is the exponent of the largest power of \(2\) dividing \(m\). Let \(x\ge3\) be odd and \(k=v_2(3x+1)\). (i) \(\log S(x)-\log x=\log(3+1/x)-k\log2\). (ii) If \(k\ge2\), then \(S(x)<x\), \(\log S(x)-\log x\le\log\bigl(\tfrac34+\tfrac1{4x}\bigr)<0\), and \(\log S(x)-\log x\le\log(7/9)\), with equality exactly at \(x=9\). (iii) If \(k=1\), which happens exactly when \(x\equiv3\pmod4\), then \(S(x)=(3x+1)/2>x\) and \(\log\tfrac32<\log S(x)-\log x=\log\bigl(\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2x}\bigr)\le\log\tfrac53\), with equality on the right exactly at \(x=3\).
Source: book/chapters/ch04_lyapunov.tex, label thm:stride.




Theorem 4.8, page 73 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(S\) be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, \(S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}\), where \(v_2(m)\) is the exponent of the largest power of \(2\) dividing \(m\). Let \(W\) be a strictly increasing function from the odd positive integers to \((0,\infty)\), and let \(\rho\le1\). Then \(W(S(x))>\rho\,W(x)\) for every \(x\equiv3\pmod4\). In particular no strictly increasing \(W\) is a strict Lyapunov function for \((S,\{1\})\) (one with \(W(S(x))<W(x)\) for every odd \(x\ne1\)) or a strong Lyapunov function for \((S,\{1\})\) (one with \(W>0\) and \(W(S(x))\le\rho W(x)\) for every odd \(x\ne1\), for some constant \(\rho<1\)), and the set of odd integers on which \(W(S(x))\le\rho W(x)\) fails contains the residue class \(3\bmod4\), which has natural density \(\tfrac12\) among the odd integers; for \(\rho=1\) the set on which it fails is exactly this class.
Source: book/chapters/ch04_lyapunov.tex, label thm:nolyapunov.




Proposition 4.12, page 74 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(S\) be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, \(S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}\), where \(v_2(m)\) is the exponent of the largest power of \(2\) dividing \(m\). For odd \(x\) write \(k_1=v_2(3x+1)\), \(k_2=v_2(3S(x)+1)\) and \(S^{(2)}(x)=S(S(x))\). Let \(x\ge3\) be odd. (i) \(S^{(2)}(x)<x\) if and only if \(k_1+k_2\ge4\). (ii) The odd integers with a two stride descent, that is with \(S^{(2)}(x)<x\), have natural density exactly \(\tfrac12\) among the odd integers. (iii) \(\max_{x\ge3\text{ odd}}\bigl(\log S^{(2)}(x)-\log x\bigr)=\log\tfrac{17}{7}\approx0.8873\), attained only at \(x=7\), where \(S(7)=11\) and \(S^{(2)}(7)=17\).
Source: book/chapters/ch04_lyapunov.tex, label prop:ch4:twostride.




Corollary 4.15, page 78 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(S\) be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, \(S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}\), where \(v_2(m)\) is the exponent of the largest power of \(2\) dividing \(m\), and let \(S^{(J)}\) be its \(J\)th iterate. Fix \(J\ge1\), \(\rho\le1\) and a strictly increasing function \(W\) from the odd positive integers to \((0,\infty)\). Then \(W(S^{(J)}(x))>\rho\,W(x)\) for every odd \(x\equiv-1\pmod{2^{J+1}}\), that is, for every \(x=2^{J+1}q-1\) with \(q\ge1\). This set is infinite and has natural density \(2^{-J}\) among the odd integers. Moreover, along it, [()^{J}(q).]
Source: book/chapters/ch04_lyapunov.tex, label cor:ch4:multistride.




Proposition 4.19, page 79 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(T_0\) be the standard Collatz map, \(T_0(x)=x/2\) for even \(x\) and \(T_0(x)=3x+1\) for odd \(x\), and let \(g(y\mid x)=\log x+(y-x)/x\) be the tangent line majorizer of \(\log\) at \(x\), so that the surrogate increment \(g(T_0(x)\mid x)-g(x\mid x)\) equals \(-\tfrac12\) for even \(x\) and \(2+1/x\) for odd \(x\). Under the stochastic model for the standard map, in which the parities of successive steps form a stationary renewal chain \((B_n)\) on \(\{0,1\}\) (with \(B_n=1\) for an odd step; an odd step is always followed by an even step, and an even step is followed by an odd or an even step with probability \(\tfrac12\) each), so that a step is odd with stationary probability \(\tfrac13\), the mean surrogate increment per step of \(T_0\) is \(\tfrac13\cdot2+\tfrac23\cdot\bigl(-\tfrac12\bigr)=+\tfrac13>0\), up to the \(O(1/x)\) term, whereas the mean true increment per step is \(\tfrac13\log3-\tfrac23\log2=\tfrac13\log(3/4)\approx-0.0959<0\). Per Syracuse stride, that is one odd step followed by \(k\) even steps, in the stride model with \(k\) distributed as Geometric\((\tfrac12)\) on \(\{1,2,\dots\}\), the per step surrogate increments summed over the stride, with the majorizer recentred at every step, have mean \(+1\) up to the \(O(1/x)\) term, and the mean true increment is \(\log(3/4)\approx-0.2877\).
Source: book/chapters/ch04_lyapunov.tex, label prop:mmfails.




Proposition 4.20, page 81 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Work in the stride model of the Collatz map, in which the log increment of one stride is \(\Delta=\log3-K\log2\) with \(K\) distributed as Geometric\((\tfrac12)\) on \(\{1,2,\dots\}\), and write \(M(p)=\mathbb{E}[e^{p\Delta}]=3^{p}/(2^{1+p}-1)\). For \(0<p\le1\) let \(g_p(y\mid x)=\log x+\frac{(y/x)^{p}-1}{p}\); each \(g_p\) dominates \(\log y\) and is tangent to it at \(y=x\), and \(p=1\) is the tangent line (linear) majorizer of \(\log\). Then the mean stride increment of the surrogate \(g_p\), ignoring the \(1/x\) correction, is \((M(p)-1)/p\), and: (i) \(M(0)=M(1)=1\), and \(M(p)<1\) for \(0<p<1\); (ii) \(p\mapsto(M(p)-1)/p\) is increasing on \((0,1]\), tends to \(\mathbb{E}[\Delta]=\log(3/4)\) as \(p\downarrow0\), and equals \(0\) at \(p=1\). In particular every power majorizer with \(0<p<1\) has strictly negative mean surrogate increment, and the linear majorizer \(p=1\) sits exactly on the boundary.
Source: book/chapters/ch04_lyapunov.tex, label prop:ch4:power.

title: Results by chapter On the Collatz Conjecture
text:
Theorem 6.3, page 101 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(T\) be the accelerated Collatz map, \(T(x)=x/2\) for even \(x\) and \(T(x)=(3x+1)/2\) for odd \(x\). Fix \(d\ge1\) and let \(G_d\) be the directed graph on the residues modulo \(2^d\) in which the residue \(a\) has an edge to each residue \(a'\) with \(a'\equiv T(a)\pmod{2^{d-1}}\) (the two lifts of \(T(a)\)), with weight \(w(a)=\log(3/2)\) if \(a\) is odd and \(w(a)=-\log2\) if \(a\) is even. (i) There are a function \(\varphi\) on \(\mathbb{Z}/2^d\mathbb{Z}\) and a bound \(X\) such that \(V(T(x))<V(x)\) for all integers \(x\ge X\), where \(V(x)=\log x+\varphi(x\bmod2^d)\), if and only if every cycle of \(G_d\) has negative total weight. (ii) For every \(d\ge1\) the graph \(G_d\) contains cycles of positive weight: the loop at \(-1\), of weight \(\log(3/2)\), and the images of the cycles of \(T\) on the negative integers, whose weights are \(r\log3-s\log2>0\) for a cycle with \(r\) odd steps among \(s\) steps. The maximum cycle mean of \(G_d\) is exactly \(\log(3/2)\) for every \(d\). (iii) Consequently no potential \(\log x+\varphi(x\bmod2^d)\) with bounded \(\varphi\) decreases at every step for all large \(x\), for any \(d\), and the same holds for potentials required to decrease over any fixed number \(J\) of steps.
Source: book/chapters/ch05c_mmcollatz.tex, label thm:ch5c:residue.




Proposition 6.4, page 102 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(S\) be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, \(S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}\), where \(v_2(m)\) is the exponent of the largest power of \(2\) dividing \(m\), and let \(V(x)=\log x+\varphi(x)\) for a real function \(\varphi\) on the odd positive integers. Suppose \(V(S(x))<V(x)\) for every odd \(x\ge3\). Then for every \(j\ge2\) and every odd \(q\ge1\), [(2jq-1)-(2{j-1}q-1);>;(j-1) .] In particular \(\varphi\) is unbounded above or below, and \(\sup\varphi-\inf\varphi\ge(j-1)\log(3/2)\) for every \(j\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05c_mmcollatz.tex, label prop:ch5c:surplus.




Proposition 6.6, page 104 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(S\) be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, \(S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{k}\) with \(k=v_2(3x+1)\), where \(v_2(m)\) is the exponent of the largest power of \(2\) dividing \(m\), let \(\varepsilon(x)=\log\bigl(1+\tfrac1{3x}\bigr)\), and for \(c>\log(3/2)\) let \(V_c(x)=\log x+c\,v_2(x+1)\). Then \(V_c\) decreases at every ascending stride (a stride with \(k=1\)) from an odd \(x>1/\bigl(2(e^c-3/2)\bigr)\), hence at every ascending stride when \(c>\log(5/3)\) and at all but finitely many when \(c\le\log(5/3)\). The descending strides (\(k\ge2\)) at which \(V_c\) fails to decrease are exactly those \(x\mapsto y=S(x)\), with \(k\) halvings, that land on a \(y\) with \(v_2(y+1)-1\ge(k\log2-\log3-\varepsilon(x))/c\). Under the stride model, in which \(k\) and \(v_2(y+1)\) are independent Geometric\((\tfrac12)\) variables on \(\{1,2,\dots\}\), the fraction of odd \(x\) at which \(V_c\) fails to decrease is [p(c)=_{k}2{-k},2{-(k-)/c},] which is \(0.2087\) at \(c=1\) and decreases to \(0.1431\) as \(c\downarrow\log(3/2)\), and \(V_c\) fails at a positive fraction of odd integers for every \(c\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05c_mmcollatz.tex, label prop:ch5c:runpot.

title: Results by chapter On the Collatz Conjecture
text:
Lemma 7.5, page 117 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(\alpha>0\), and write \(G_h(x)=x-h\nabla f(x)\) for a gradient step of length \(h\). Switching MM with step \(\alpha\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\) starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain gradient step \(x_{t+1}=G_\alpha(x_t)\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=G_\alpha(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\). Let \(t\) be even. Then \(x_{t+1}=G_\alpha(x_t)\), and the extrapolated point at the following odd iteration is \(y_{t+1}=x_{t+1}+\beta(x_{t+1}-x_t)=x_t-(1+\beta)\alpha\nabla f(x_t)=G_{(1+\beta)\alpha}(x_t)\). Consequently \(x_{t+2}=G_\alpha\bigl(G_{(1+\beta)\alpha}(x_t)\bigr)\), and in the form that exhibits the momentum, \(x_{t+2}=x_{t+1}-\beta\alpha\nabla f(x_t)-\alpha\nabla f(y_{t+1})\).
Source: book/chapters/ch06_smm.tex, label lem:ch6:ystep.




Theorem 7.6, page 118 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x\) with \(A\) symmetric positive definite and minimizer \(x^\ast=A^{-1}b\), let \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), write \(G_h(x)=x-h\nabla f(x)\), and let \((x_t)\) be generated by Switching MM with step \(\alpha\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\) (it starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain gradient step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\)). For every even \(t\ge0\), \(x_{t+2}=G_{(1+\beta)\alpha}(x_{t+1})=G_{(1+\beta)\alpha}\bigl(G_\alpha(x_t)\bigr)\), that is, two steps of Switching MM from an even index are a gradient step of length \(\alpha\) followed by a gradient step of length \((1+\beta)\alpha\), and every iterate of Switching MM is an iterate of this cyclic schedule. In terms of the error \(e_t=x_t-x^\ast\), \(e_{t+2}=(I-\alpha A)\bigl(I-(1+\beta)\alpha A\bigr)e_t\) for even \(t\).
Source: book/chapters/ch06_smm.tex, label thm:smmquad.




Corollary 7.8, page 119 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x\) with \(A\) symmetric positive definite whose largest eigenvalue is \(L\), let \(\alpha>0\) and \(0\le\beta<1\), and let Switching MM with step \(\alpha\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\) (it starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain gradient step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\)) have the two step multiplier \(\rho(a)=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)=1-(2+\beta)a+(1+\beta)a^2\) on an eigendirection with eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\). Then for real \(a\), \(|\rho(a)|<1\) if and only if \(0<a<(2+\beta)/(1+\beta)\). In particular Switching MM converges linearly on every strongly convex quadratic whenever \(\alpha\le1/L\), and in fact whenever \(\alpha L<(2+\beta)/(1+\beta)\). For all \(a>0\), \(\rho(a)\ge1-(2+\beta)^2/\bigl(4(1+\beta)\bigr)\), a minimum attained at \(a=(2+\beta)/\bigl(2(1+\beta)\bigr)\).
Source: book/chapters/ch06_smm.tex, label cor:ch6:stability.




Corollary 7.9, page 120 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x\) with \(A\) symmetric positive definite, let \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), and let Switching MM with step \(\alpha\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\) (it starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain gradient step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\)) have the two step multiplier \(\rho(a)=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)\) on an eigendirection with eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\) (that is, the error component along that eigenvector satisfies \(e_{t+2}=\rho(a)e_t\) for even \(t\)). As \(a\to0\), \(\rho(a)=1-(2+\beta)a+O(a^2)\), and the per step contraction factor \(|\rho(a)|^{1/2}\) equals \(1-\tfrac{2+\beta}{2}a+O(a^2)\). Thus in the slow directions Switching MM behaves like gradient descent with the effective step \(m_{\mathrm{SMM}}\,\alpha\), where \(m_{\mathrm{SMM}}=\tfrac{2+\beta}{2}\), which is \(1.2925\) at \(\beta=\log_23-1\).
Source: book/chapters/ch06_smm.tex, label cor:ch6:slow.




Proposition 7.10, page 122 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice differentiable with \(\nabla^2f\) Lipschitz with constant \(M\) (in the Euclidean and induced operator norms), let \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), write \(G_h(x)=x-h\nabla f(x)\), and let \((x_t)\) be generated by Switching MM with step \(\alpha\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\) (it starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain gradient step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\)). For even \(t\), with \(h=x_{t+1}-x_t=-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)\), \(x_{t+2}-G_{(1+\beta)\alpha}(x_{t+1})=\alpha\bigl[(1+\beta)\nabla f(x_{t+1})-\beta\nabla f(x_{t+1}-h)-\nabla f(x_{t+1}+\beta h)\bigr]\), and \(\bigl\|x_{t+2}-G_{(1+\beta)\alpha}(x_{t+1})\bigr\|\le\tfrac{M}{2}\,\beta(1+\beta)\,\alpha^3\,\|\nabla f(x_t)\|^2\). The bracket vanishes identically when \(\nabla f\) is affine.
Source: book/chapters/ch06_smm.tex, label prop:ch6:defect.

title: Results by chapter On the Collatz Conjecture
text:
Theorem 8.4, page 128 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x\) with \(A\) symmetric positive definite and minimizer \(x^\ast\), and suppose the algorithm sees the noisy gradient \(g(x)=\nabla f(x)+\xi\), where a fresh \(\xi\) is drawn at every call, independent of the past, with mean zero and covariance \(\sigma^2I\). Run Switching MM with step \(\alpha>0\) and momentum coefficient \(0\le\beta<1\) with \(g\) in place of \(\nabla f\) (it starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha g(x_t)\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha g(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\)). Fix an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(A\) with normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\in(0,1]\), let \(e_t\) be the component of \(x_t-x^\ast\) along its eigenvector and \(\xi_t\) the component of the noise drawn at iteration \(t\) (independent, mean zero, variance \(\sigma^2\)), and put \(\rho=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)\). (i) For every even \(t\), \(e_{t+2}=\rho\,e_t+w_t\) with \(w_t=-(1-a)(1+\beta)\alpha\,\xi_t-\alpha\,\xi_{t+1}\), where the \(w_t\) for even \(t\) are independent, independent of \(e_t\), with mean zero and \(\operatorname{Var}(w_t)=\alpha^2\sigma^2\bigl[(1-a)^2(1+\beta)^2+1\bigr]\). (ii) As \(t\to\infty\) through even values, \(\operatorname{Var}(e_t)\) converges to \(V_{\mathrm{even}}=\alpha^2\sigma^2\bigl[(1-a)^2(1+\beta)^2+1\bigr]/(1-\rho^2)\), and through odd values to \(V_{\mathrm{odd}}=(1-a)^2V_{\mathrm{even}}+\alpha^2\sigma^2\). (iii) The phase averaged stationary variance \(V_{\mathrm{SMM}}=\tfrac12(V_{\mathrm{even}}+V_{\mathrm{odd}})\) satisfies \(V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)/(\alpha^2\sigma^2)=Q(a,\beta)/(1-\rho^2)\), where \(Q(a,\beta)=(2+2\beta+\beta^2)-(1+\beta)(2+3\beta)\,a+(1+\beta)(1+3\beta)\,a^2-\beta(1+\beta)\,a^3\) and \(1-\rho^2=a\bigl(2+\beta-(1+\beta)a\bigr)\bigl(2-(2+\beta)a+(1+\beta)a^2\bigr)\).
Source: book/chapters/ch07_noise.tex, label thm:smmvar.




Corollary 8.5, page 129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x\) with \(A\) symmetric positive definite, with the noisy gradient oracle \(g(x)=\nabla f(x)+\xi\) (a fresh \(\xi\) at every call, independent of the past, mean zero, covariance \(\sigma^2I\)), and run Switching MM with step \(\alpha>0\) and momentum coefficient \(0\le\beta<1\) with \(g\) in place of \(\nabla f\) (plain step at even \(t\), extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha g(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\) at odd \(t\)). On the eigendirection of an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) with normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\in(0,1]\), let \(V_{\mathrm{even}}\) and \(V_{\mathrm{odd}}\) be the limits of the variance of the error component along even and odd times, \(V_{\mathrm{SMM}}=\tfrac12(V_{\mathrm{even}}+V_{\mathrm{odd}})\), and \(V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)=\alpha^2\sigma^2/\bigl(a(2-a)\bigr)\) the stationary variance of noisy gradient descent \(e_{t+1}=(1-a)e_t-\alpha\xi_t\) with the same step. As \(a\to0\), both \(aV_{\mathrm{even}}\) and \(aV_{\mathrm{odd}}\) converge to \(\alpha^2\sigma^2\,\dfrac{(1+\beta)^2+1}{2(2+\beta)}=\alpha^2\sigma^2\,\dfrac{1+\beta+\beta^2/2}{2+\beta}\). Consequently \(\lim_{a\to0}V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)/V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)=V(\beta):=\dfrac{2+2\beta+\beta^2}{2+\beta}=\beta+\dfrac{2}{2+\beta}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch07_noise.tex, label cor:ch7:slow.




Proposition 8.7, page 130 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x\) with \(A\) symmetric positive definite, with the noisy gradient oracle \(g(x)=\nabla f(x)+\xi\) (a fresh \(\xi\) at every call, independent of the past, mean zero, covariance \(\sigma^2I\)), and run Switching MM with step \(\alpha>0\) and momentum coefficient \(0\le\beta<1\) with \(g\) in place of \(\nabla f\). On the eigendirection of an eigenvalue \(\lambda\) with normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\in(0,1]\), let \(V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)\) be the phase averaged stationary variance of the error component (the average of its limits along even and odd times), \(V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)=\alpha^2\sigma^2/\bigl(a(2-a)\bigr)\) the stationary variance of noisy gradient descent with the same step, and \(V(\beta)=\beta+2/(2+\beta)\). Then for \(0\le\beta<1\) and every \(a\in(0,1]\), \(V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)\le V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)\le V(\beta)\,V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)<\tfrac53\,V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)\), with \(V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)=V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)\) only when \(\beta=0\) or \(a=1\), and \(V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)=V(\beta)\,V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)\) only when \(\beta=0\).
Source: book/chapters/ch07_noise.tex, label prop:ch7:uniform.




Proposition 8.9, page 132 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider noisy gradient methods on a strongly convex quadratic with additive gradient noise of variance \(\sigma^2\) and step \(\alpha\), in the slow mode limit \(a=\alpha\lambda\to0\) along an eigendirection. A method has the effective step multiplier \(m\) if its slow mode contracts like gradient descent with step \(m\alpha\) (and gradient descent with step \(m\alpha\) has slow mode variance \(m\) times that at step \(\alpha\)), and the slow mode variance amplification \(V\) if its stationary variance is \(V\) times that of gradient descent at step \(\alpha\). Its noise floor at matched speed relative to gradient descent is \(V/m\). For momentum coefficient \(0\le\beta<1\), this equals \(1\) for every step heavy ball and for every step Nesterov momentum (where \(V=m=1/(1-\beta)\)), and for Switching MM (where \(m=(2+\beta)/2\) and \(V=(2+2\beta+\beta^2)/(2+\beta)\)) it equals \(\dfrac{2(2+2\beta+\beta^2)}{(2+\beta)^2}=1+\dfrac{\beta^2}{(2+\beta)^2}\ge1\), which is \(1.051\) at \(\beta=\log_23-1\) and increases to \(10/9\) as \(\beta\to1\). More generally, for any period two cyclic gradient step schedule with steps \(h_1\alpha\) and \(h_2\alpha\) the ratio is \(\tfrac12(h_1^2+h_2^2)\big/\bigl(\tfrac12(h_1+h_2)\bigr)^2\ge1\), with equality only for equal steps.
Source: book/chapters/ch07_noise.tex, label prop:ch7:matched.




Theorem 8.12, page 135 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Fix a period \(p\ge1\) and a memory length \(K\ge1\). On one eigendirection of a quadratic with normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\), with the state \(z_t=(e_t,\dots,e_{t-K+1})\) of past errors, a linear periodic first order method evaluates at step \(t\), with residue \(j=t\bmod p\), the gradient at the extrapolated point \(y_t=\gamma_j\cdot z_t\) and updates \(e_{t+1}=\delta_j\cdot z_t-h_j\bigl(a\,y_t+\alpha\xi_t\bigr)\), where \(\gamma_j,\delta_j\in\mathbb{R}^K\) and the step multipliers \(h_j>0\) are fixed, and the gradient noise \(\xi_t\) has mean zero, is uncorrelated across steps and has variance \(\sigma^2\). Consistency requires \(\delta_j\cdot\iota=\gamma_j\cdot\iota=1\) for \(\iota=(1,\dots,1)\). Let \(S_j(a)\) be the step matrix mapping \(z_t\) to \(z_{t+1}\) without noise (its first row is \((\delta_j-a\,h_j\gamma_j)^\top\) and its other rows shift the entries of \(z_t\) down by one place), and write the product of the \(p\) step matrices of one period as \(B(a)=B_0+aB_1+O(a^2)\). Assume the method is stable at \(a=0\): the eigenvalue \(1\) of \(B_0\), with right eigenvector \(\iota\), is simple and all other eigenvalues of \(B_0\) lie strictly inside the unit disc. Let \(w\) be the left eigenvector of \(B_0\) for the eigenvalue \(1\) with \(w\cdot\iota=1\). The gain of the \(i\)th step of the period is \(c_i=h_i\,w\cdot\Pi_iu_1\), where \(u_1\) is the first unit vector and \(\Pi_i\) is the product, at \(a=0\), of the step matrices of steps \(i+1,\dots,p\) of the period, and \(M=\sum_{i=1}^pc_i\), which is assumed to be positive. Then, as \(a\to0\): (i) the per step contraction of the slow mode is \(1-(M/p)\,a+O(a^2)\); (ii) the phase averaged stationary variance of \(e_t\) is \(\alpha^2\sigma^2\,\dfrac{\sum_ic_i^2}{2Ma}\,(1+o(1))\); (iii) consequently the noise floor relative to gradient descent run at the same slow mode speed, with step \((M/p)\alpha\), is \(\mathcal F=\dfrac{p\sum_{i=1}^pc_i^2}{\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^pc_i\bigr)^2}\ge1\), with equality if and only if all gains are equal.
Source: book/chapters/ch07_noise.tex, label thm:ch7:gainweight.




Proposition 8.14, page 137 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f\) be a quadratic whose Hessian has its spectrum in \([\mu,L]\), with \(\kappa=L/\mu\), and consider gradient descent with cyclic steps \(h_1,h_2\) (alternating absolute step lengths) of ratio \(r=h_2/h_1\ge1\), under additive gradient noise. Put \(G(r)=\dfrac{(1+r)^2}{4r}\ge1\). The worst case two step contraction over \([\mu,L]\) is \(\max_{\lambda\in[\mu,L]}|(1-h_1\lambda)(1-h_2\lambda)|\), and the slow mode noise floor at matched speed is the slow mode stationary variance divided by that of gradient descent with the constant step of the same slow mode speed. (i) The slow mode noise floor at matched speed is \(N=\dfrac{2(h_1^2+h_2^2)}{(h_1+h_2)^2}=2-\dfrac1{G(r)}\). (ii) For fixed \(r\) with \(G(r)\le G_{\mathrm{ch}}(\kappa)=\dfrac{2(\kappa+1)^2}{\kappa^2+6\kappa+1}\), the smallest possible worst case two step contraction over \([\mu,L]\) is \(R^\ast(r)=1-\dfrac{4\kappa\,G(r)}{(\kappa+1)^2}\), attained when the steps are scaled so that \(h_1+h_2=4G(r)/(\mu+L)\). For \(G(r)>G_{\mathrm{ch}}(\kappa)\) the smallest worst case contraction exceeds that of the Chebyshev ratio. (iii) Consequently the Pareto frontier between rate and noise floor is \(R=1-\dfrac{4\kappa}{(2-N)(\kappa+1)^2}\) for \(1\le N\le N_{\mathrm{ch}}(\kappa)\), where \(N_{\mathrm{ch}}=\dfrac{3\kappa^2+2\kappa+3}{2(\kappa+1)^2}\) is the noise floor of the two step Chebyshev schedule (the period two schedule minimizing the worst case two step contraction over \([\mu,L]\)), whose ratio tends to \((1+\sqrt2)^2=5.83\) and whose floor tends to \(3/2\) as \(\kappa\to\infty\).
Source: book/chapters/ch07_noise.tex, label prop:ch7:pareto.




Proposition 8.15, page 141 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Consider on one eigendirection of a quadratic with eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\) the oracle \(g(y)=(\lambda+\eta_t)\,e_y+\xi_t\) for the gradient at a point with error \(e_y\) along that eigenvector, where \(\eta_t,\xi_t\) are independent of the past, with mean zero, uncorrelated with each other, \(\operatorname{Var}(\alpha\eta_t)=\omega^2\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\xi_t)=\sigma^2\). For Switching MM with step \(\alpha\) and momentum coefficient \(0\le\beta<1\) the second moments of the error obey a closed linear recursion: with \(\nu_1=(1-a)^2+\omega^2\) and \(\nu_2=\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)^2+(1+\beta)^2\omega^2\), the stationary second moment at even times is \(\alpha^2\sigma^2\bigl(\nu_1(1+\beta)^2+1\bigr)/(1-\nu_1\nu_2)\), finite if and only if \(\nu_1\nu_2<1\). As \(a\to0\): (i) under the least squares scaling \(\omega^2=\vartheta a^2\) with \(\vartheta\) fixed (the relative curvature noise, \(\vartheta=2\) for a Gaussian regressor), the slow mode ratio of the stationary second moment of Switching MM to that of gradient descent with the same step and noise is unchanged, equal to \((2+2\beta+\beta^2)/(2+\beta)\) for every \(\vartheta\); (ii) under the diffusive scaling \(\omega^2=\epsilon a\), for any linear periodic first order method of period \(p\) on this eigendirection (with state \(z_t=(e_t,\dots,e_{t-K+1})\) and residue \(j=t\bmod p\) it sets \(e_{t+1}=\delta_j\cdot z_t-h_j\alpha\bigl((\lambda+\eta_t)y_t+\xi_t\bigr)\) with \(y_t=\gamma_j\cdot z_t\), where \(\gamma_j,\delta_j\in\mathbb{R}^K\) with \(\gamma_j\cdot\iota=\delta_j\cdot\iota=1\) for \(\iota=(1,\dots,1)\) and \(h_j>0\) are fixed) that is stable at \(a=0\) (the product \(B_0\) of its step matrices over one period at \(a=0\) has the simple eigenvalue \(1\) and all its other eigenvalues strictly inside the unit disc) and has \(M>0\), where \(c_i=h_i\,w\cdot\Pi_iu_1\) is the gain of step \(i\) (\(w\) the left eigenvector of \(B_0\) for the eigenvalue \(1\) with \(w\cdot\iota=1\), \(u_1\) the first unit vector, \(\Pi_i\) the product at \(a=0\) of the step matrices of steps \(i+1,\dots,p\)) and \(M=\sum_ic_i\), the stationary second moment of the error satisfies \(a\,\mathbb{E}[e^2]\to\alpha^2\sigma^2\sum_ic_i^2\big/\bigl(2M-\epsilon\sum_ic_i^2\bigr)\), so that the method is mean square stable for small \(a\) exactly when \(\epsilon<\epsilon^\ast=2M/\sum_ic_i^2\).
Source: book/chapters/ch07_noise.tex, label prop:ch7:mult.

title: Results by chapter On the Collatz Conjecture
text:
Theorem 9.3, page 158 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(T\) be the accelerated Collatz map, \(T(n)=n/2\) for even \(n\) and \(T(n)=(3n+1)/2\) for odd \(n\). For an integer \(n\not\equiv0\pmod 3\) and \(X\ge1\) let \(\pi_n(X)=\#\{m\le Xn:\ \text{the orbit of }m\text{ under }T\text{ passes through }n\}\). For an integer \(j\ge1\) and \(n\not\equiv0\pmod3\) with \(2^jn\equiv2\pmod3\) put \(c_j(n)=(2^{j+1}n-1)/3\), the odd preimage of \(2^jn\), and call \(j\) fertile for \(n\) if \(2^jn\equiv2\) or \(8\pmod9\). Fix \(k\ge1\) and let \(\mathcal R_k\) be the set of residues modulo \(3^k\) prime to \(3\). For \(g>0\) and a positive vector \((w_r)_{r\in\mathcal R_k}\) define \((\Phi_gw)_r=\min_{\ell}\sum_{j\ \mathrm{fertile\ for}\ \ell}\bigl(3/2^{j+1}\bigr)^g\,w_{[c_j(\ell)]}\), where the minimum is over the three lifts \(\ell\) of \(r\) to residues modulo \(3^{k+1}\), the sum is over all \(j\ge1\), and fertility of \(j\) and the class \([c_j(\ell)]\in\mathcal R_k\) (the residue of \(c_j(n)\) modulo \(3^k\) for any integer \(n\equiv\ell\)) depend only on \(\ell\) and \(j\). If \(\Phi_gw\ge(1+\eta)w\) componentwise for some \(\eta>0\), then there is \(C>0\) such that \(\pi_n(X)\ge C\,w_{[n]}\,X^g\) for all \(X\ge1\) and all \(n\not\equiv0\pmod3\) not lying on a cycle of \(T\), where \([n]\) is the residue of \(n\) modulo \(3^k\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label thm:ch5b:exponent.




Corollary 9.4, page 159 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For all sufficiently large \(x\), at least \(x^{0.477}\) integers \(m\le x\) have orbits under the accelerated Collatz map \(T\) (\(T(n)=n/2\) for even \(n\) and \(T(n)=(3n+1)/2\) for odd \(n\)) that reach \(1\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label cor:ch5b:count.




Proposition 9.5, page 161 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L\) smooth (its gradient is Lipschitz with constant \(L\)) and bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\), and run Switching MM with step \(1/L\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\in[0,1)\) (it starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain gradient step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\nabla f(x_t)/L\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\nabla f(y_t)/L\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\)). For even \(t\), \(f(x_{t+2})\le f(x_t)-\dfrac{1-\beta^2}{2L}\|\nabla f(x_t)\|^2-\dfrac1{2L}\|\nabla f(y_{t+1})\|^2\), where \(y_{t+1}=x_{t+1}+\beta(x_{t+1}-x_t)\). Consequently \(\min_{t<2K,\ t\ \mathrm{even}}\|\nabla f(x_t)\|^2\le\dfrac{2L\bigl(f(x_0)-f_{\inf}\bigr)}{(1-\beta^2)K}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label prop:ch5b:monotone.




Proposition 9.6, page 162 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. For parameters \(a\) and \(\beta\) (in Switching MM on an eigendirection of a quadratic, \(a=\alpha\lambda>0\) and \(0\le\beta<1\)), let \(D=\begin{pmatrix}1-a&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) and \(N=\begin{pmatrix}(1-a)(1+\beta)&-(1-a)\beta\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) be the matrices that map the state \((e_t,e_{t-1})\) to \((e_{t+1},e_t)\) for a descent step and for an injection step, and let \(\hat\rho(\{D,N\})=\lim_{k\to\infty}\max_{M_i\in\{D,N\}}\|M_k\cdots M_1\|^{1/k}\) be their joint spectral radius. Write \(D=vu^\top\) with \(u=(1,0)^\top\) and \(v=(1-a,1)^\top\), and put \(\tau_j=u^\top N^jv\) for \(j\ge0\). Then \(\hat\rho(\{D,N\})=\max\Bigl(\rho(N),\ \sup_{j\ge0}|\tau_j|^{1/(j+1)}\Bigr)\), where \(\rho(N)\) is the spectral radius of \(N\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label prop:ch5b:jsr.




Conjecture 9.7, page 163 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(N=\begin{pmatrix}(1-a)(1+\beta)&-(1-a)\beta\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), \(u=(1,0)^\top\) and \(v=(1-a,1)^\top\), and let \(\tau_j=u^\top N^jv\) for \(j\ge0\) (the first coordinate after \(j\) injection steps of Switching MM, with normalized step \(a\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\), started from the state left by one descent step). Conjecture: for all \(a\in(0,1]\), \(\beta\in[0,1)\) and \(j\ge0\), \(|\tau_j|\le1-a\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label conj:ch5b:transient.




Corollary 9.8, page 163 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the transient bound \(|\tau_j|<1\) for every \(j\ge0\) at the fixed normalized step \(a\), where \(\tau_j=u^\top N^jv\) is defined in the statement; it is the content of the transient bound conjecture (\(|\tau_j|\le1-a\) for all \(a\in(0,1]\), \(\beta\in[0,1)\) and \(j\ge0\)), which has been checked numerically on a finite grid of parameters and is not proved.
Statement. Let \(0\le\beta<1\) and fix \(a\in(0,1)\). On an eigendirection of a quadratic with eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and normalized step \(a=\alpha\lambda\), let \(D(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1-a&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) and \(N(a)=\begin{pmatrix}(1-a)(1+\beta)&-(1-a)\beta\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) be the matrices that map the state \((e_t,e_{t-1})\) to \((e_{t+1},e_t)\) for a descent step and for an injection step of Switching MM, let \(\hat\rho(\{D(a),N(a)\})\) be their joint spectral radius, and let \(\tau_j=u^\top N(a)^jv\) with \(u=(1,0)^\top\) and \(v=(1-a,1)^\top\). Suppose \(|\tau_j|<1\) for all \(j\ge0\). Then on a quadratic with spectrum in \((0,L]\) and step \(\alpha=1/L\), every switching sequence between descent and injection steps, whether periodic, random, or chosen adaptively from the state, converges to the minimizer on the eigendirection with \(a=\alpha\lambda\), with exponential rate at most \(\hat\rho(\{D(a),N(a)\})<1\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label cor:ch5b:anyswitch.




Theorem 9.9, page 164 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f\) be \(\mu\) strongly convex and \(L\) smooth with minimizer \(x^\ast\), put \(\kappa=L/\mu\), and run Switching MM with step \(\alpha=1/L\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\in[0,1)\) (it starts from \(x_{-1}=x_0\), takes the plain gradient step \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)\) at even \(t\), and at odd \(t\) takes the extrapolated step \(x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)\) with \(y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})\)). For every even \(t\), \(\|x_{t+2}-x^\ast\|\le q\,\|x_t-x^\ast\|\) with \(q=q(\beta,\kappa)=\Bigl(1-\dfrac1\kappa\Bigr)\max\Bigl(1-\dfrac{1+\beta}{\kappa},\ \beta\Bigr)\), and \(f(x_{t+2})-f^\ast\le q^2\,\bigl(f(x_t)-f^\ast\bigr)\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label thm:ch5b:rate.




Corollary 9.10, page 165 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f\) be \(\mu\) strongly convex and \(L\) smooth with condition number \(\kappa=L/\mu\), run Switching MM with step \(1/L\) and momentum coefficient \(\beta\in[0,1)\), and let \(q=(1-1/\kappa)\max\bigl(1-(1+\beta)/\kappa,\ \beta\bigr)\) be the worst case, over this class of functions, of the factor by which two steps contract the distance to the minimizer. For \(\kappa\ge(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)\) the per step rate of Switching MM is \(q^{1/2}=\bigl((1-1/\kappa)(1-(1+\beta)/\kappa)\bigr)^{1/2}\), so that \(-\kappa\log q^{1/2}\to(2+\beta)/2\) as \(\kappa\to\infty\), against \(1\) for gradient descent with the same step.
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label cor:ch5b:speed.




Proposition 9.11, page 165 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), On the Collatz Conjecture: Martingales, Momentum and Continued Fractions, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) be three times differentiable, write \(G_h(x)=x-h\nabla f(x)\), and consider the composition of gradient steps of lengths \(h_1\) and \(h_2\), in either order. To second order in \(h=h_1+h_2\) (that is, up to terms of order \(h^3\)) it agrees with the time \(h\) flow of the modified equation \(\dot x=-\nabla f(x)-\dfrac{h_1^2+h_2^2}{2(h_1+h_2)}\,\nabla^2f(x)\nabla f(x)=-\nabla\Bigl(f+\dfrac{\bar h}{4}\|\nabla f\|^2\Bigr)\), where \(\bar h=\dfrac{h_1^2+h_2^2}{h_1+h_2}\).
Source: book/chapters/ch05b_difference.tex, label prop:ch5b:modified.

title: Books
text:
Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov. 2026. Edition 1.
Why the Collatz (3x+1) conjecture resists proof: the map as a random walk, an optimizer and a Diophantine problem; proofs that fixed horizon monotone Lyapunov certificates and finite residue sieves cannot settle it and the cycle inequality cannot exclude all cycles; a momentum method from log2 3.

title: Computing the Riemann Hypothesis Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times
text:
Description
The Riemann Hypothesis can be restated as the positivity of a measure, the Thorin measure of a ratio of values of Riemann’s Xi function. This book computes that measure from Pólya’s integral for Xi, without primes or a list of zeros, in certified ball arithmetic, and asks what such computations can and cannot teach about the zeros.
A certified zero off the critical line would refute the hypothesis, but no finite computation can prove it. From the zeros verified up to height 3 × 10^12 the book certifies that the derivatives of the heat trace have the predicted signs up to order 1.16 × 10^25, and proves that such finite positivity tests cannot settle it: a perturbation of Xi with the same zeros below a large height, and zeros off the line above it, passes them. No proof of the hypothesis is claimed.
New results: the reciprocal Xi function at x to the power p is hyperbolically completely monotone exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi; at the basepoint one the Thorin density is certified smallest at the origin, so the shifted clock is a stable variable plus a generalized gamma convolution; between the basepoints one half and one the shifted clocks are almost generalized gamma convolutions, unconditionally; the clock of Pólya’s Bessel function is the hitting time of an explicit diffusion; adjacent real zeros of a polynomial cannot meet under the backward heat flow before an explicit time; and the Pólya law lies within 2 × 10^-6 in total variation of the ferromagnetic laws of Lee and Yang, a distance that is zero exactly under the hypothesis.
An appendix lists the scripts and data files behind the tables and figures, which are in the book’s repository https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh.

title: Computing the Riemann Hypothesis Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times
Computing the Riemann Hypothesis Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times
text:
Main results

Bosch type theorem for the reciprocal Xi function (Theorem 4.3.6, page 94): The reciprocal Xi function composed with the power x to the p is HCM exactly when the absolute value of p is at most one minus twice the largest zero angle over pi, so RH is the extreme case p equal to one.
Derivative signs of the heat trace up to order 1.16 x 10^25 (Theorem 5.1.10, page 136): From the verification of RH to height 3 times 10^12, every derivative of the heat trace alternates in sign, equivalently the Williamson measures are positive, up to order 1.16 times 10^25, with the numerical inequalities of the proof certified in ball arithmetic.
Biane form lower bound for the collision time of zeros under the backward heat flow (Theorem 8.4.8, page 279): While all zeros of a real polynomial stay real and simple, a gap between two adjacent zeros cannot close under the backward heat flow before the time one over the minimum of Laguerre’s quantity over the gap, a bound at least as strong as the one from the critical point and attained by z squared minus a squared.
Clock of Pólya’s Bessel function as a hitting time of an explicit diffusion (Theorem 8.7.10, page 357): The index side clock of Pólya’s Bessel function, the GGC with Thorin atoms at the squares of the positive zeros of nu maps to K_{i nu}(2 pi), is the clock of a hitting time of a level by an explicit diffusion, planar Brownian motion killed at rate one half and Doob transformed by K_0.
Minimum of the Thorin density at the origin and stable summand at the basepoint one (Proposition 9.1.4, page 385): With no hypothesis on the zeros, certified with the first 1800 zeros in ball arithmetic and explicit zero counts above height 2000, the Thorin density of the shifted clock at the basepoint one is smallest only at the origin, so the clock is the sum of an independent positive stable one half variable and a generalized gamma convolution.
Almost GGC theorem for the shifted clocks (Theorem 11.4.2, page 541): With no hypothesis, for every basepoint between one half and one the Cauchy kernels of the zeros to the right of the basepoint carry a vanishing fraction of the mass of the kernels of the other zeros, with a power saving from zero density estimates.
Total variation distance from the Pólya law to ferromagnetic laws is below two millionths, with no hypothesis (Proposition 13.4.6, page 639): With no hypothesis the total variation distance from the Pólya law to the ferromagnetic laws is below 1.932 × 10^-6 by a certified computation in ball arithmetic and below 1.266 × 10^-4 by an explicit construction, and it is zero exactly when the Riemann Hypothesis holds.
Threshold theorem along the flow for the shifted clocks of the heat flow function (Theorem 15.2.3, page 700): For every time \(t\ge0\) and basepoint \(\alpha\ge\frac12\), the shifted clock of the heat flow function \(\xi_t\) is the Laplace transform of a generalized gamma convolution exactly when no zero of \(\xi_t\) has real part above \(\alpha\), and its Thorin measure is then an explicit sum of Cauchy kernels and atoms over the zeros.
Phase diagram theorem, de Bruijn’s strip theorem in Thorin form (Theorem 15.3.2, page 702): The set of points \((t,\alpha)\) where the shifted clock of the heat flow function is a generalized gamma convolution is carried along parabolas by the flow (de Bruijn’s strip theorem in Thorin form), the de Bruijn Newman constant is the minimum of \(t+2(\alpha-\frac12)^2\) over it, and RH holds exactly when the corner \((0,\frac12)\) belongs to it.

title: Results by chapter Computing the Riemann Hypothesis
text:
The results of Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times that are new in the book, that come from the authors’ own papers, or that correct one of those papers, as the book states them: 278 entries (203 proved, 11 conditional, 61 open, 3 counterexample). Results of other authors that the book presents are credited in the chapter summaries.
Status: proved; conditional (proved assuming the named statements, which the book does not prove); open (stated as an open question); counterexample (a proved counterexample); withdrawn (found wrong after release; the entry says what was wrong and which version corrects it).





Proposition 1.2.1, page 12 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert’s 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\frac12 s(s - 1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be the completed zeta function, an entire function whose zeros are the nontrivial zeros of \(\zeta\), and put \(G(u)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt{u})/\xi(\frac12)\), an entire function of \(u\). The clock is the function \(1/G\). A random variable \(H\ge 0\) is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if \(\mathbb{E}\,e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\) for \(u>0\), with a drift \(d\ge 0\) and a positive measure \(U\) on \((0,\infty)\), the Thorin measure, such that \(\int_{(0,1)}|\log z|\,U(dz)+\int_{(1,\infty)}z^{-1}U(dz)<\infty\); the drift and the Thorin measure are unique. Then \(1/G\) is the Laplace transform of a GGC if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds, that is, if and only if every zero of \(\xi\) has real part \(\frac12\). In that case the drift is zero, the Thorin measure is \(U_{\mathrm{RH}}=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_{\gamma^2}\), where \(\frac12+i\gamma\) runs over the zeros of \(\xi\) with \(\gamma>0\), counted with multiplicity, and the clock variable is \(T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2\) with independent standard exponential random variables \(e_\gamma\).
Source: ch/ch02.tex, label prop:rigid.




Theorem 1.2.2, page 17 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert’s 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed zeta function, and for real \(\alpha\) and real \(r\) put \(v_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+ir)\). If \(\alpha>\operatorname{Re}\rho\) for every zero \(\rho\) of \(\xi\), in particular for every \(\alpha\ge 1\), then \(u\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})\) is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution \(T_\alpha\) (a random variable \(H\ge 0\) with \(\mathbb{E}\,e^{-uH}=\exp\{-du-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+u/z)\,U(dz)\}\) for \(u>0\), a drift \(d\ge 0\) and a positive Thorin measure \(U\)) whose Thorin measure has density \(v_\alpha(\sqrt{z})/(2\pi\sqrt{z})\) with respect to \(dz\) on \((0,\infty)\), and \(v_\alpha>0\). The function \(u\mapsto\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})\) is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution if and only if \(\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho\).
Source: ch/ch02.tex, label thm:poisson.




Remark 1.2.4, page 18 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed zeta function and, for real \(\alpha>\frac12\) and real \(r\), put \(v_\alpha(r)=\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\alpha+ir)\), so that \(v_\alpha(r)/\pi\) is the Thorin density at resolution \(\alpha - \frac12\). If some zero of \(\xi\) has real part greater than \(\alpha\), the shifted clock \(\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt{u})\) is not the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution. The question is whether, without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, \(v_\alpha(r)\ge 0\) for all real \(r\) implies that \(\xi\) has no zero with real part greater than \(\alpha\). The book states that this is not known for \(\xi\). What is known is that if \(v_\alpha\ge 0\) for every \(\alpha>\sigma_0\) then no zero has real part greater than \(\sigma_0\) (for \(\sigma_0=\frac12\) this is Lagarias’s criterion for RH), and that for an explicit entire function with the order, symmetry and reality of \(\xi\) the answer is negative.
Source: ch/ch02.tex, label rem:ch2:oneline.







Proposition 2.1.1, page 34 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge 1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2} - 3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})\) be the Pólya kernel, an even function that is analytic in the strip \(|\operatorname{Im}u|<\pi/4\), and let \(\xi\) be the completed zeta function, so that \(\xi(\frac12+s)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{su}\,du\). Let \(0<\delta<\pi/4\) and \(\eta=\pi/4 - \delta\). Then for every complex \(s\), \(\xi(\frac12+s)=e^{i\eta s}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(x+i\eta)\,e^{sx}\,dx\) and \(\xi'(\frac12+s)=e^{i\eta s}\int_{\mathbb{R}}(x+i\eta)\,\Phi(x+i\eta)\,e^{sx}\,dx\). For real \(x\), \(|\Phi(x+i\eta)|\le C_\delta\) and \(|(x+i\eta)\Phi(x+i\eta)|\le C_\delta\), with \(C_\delta=O(\delta^{-5/2})\) as \(\delta\to 0\).
Source: ch/ch04.tex, label prop:tilt.







Proposition 3.2.2, page 58 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed zeta function, \(\Xi(\theta)=\xi(\frac12+i\theta)\), and for \(\varepsilon>0\) let \(\mu_\varepsilon\) be the signed measure on \((0,\infty)\) whose density in the variable \(\theta=\sqrt{z}\) is the Thorin density \(\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)\), so that \(\mu_\varepsilon((0,\Theta^2])=\int_0^\Theta\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)\,d\theta\). Let \(N(\Theta)\) be the number of zeros \(\rho\) of \(\xi\) with \(0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le\Theta\), counted with multiplicity. Suppose that \(\Theta\) is not the ordinate of a zero and that every zero with \(0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le\Theta\) lies on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\). Then \(\mu_\varepsilon((0,\Theta^2])=N(\Theta) - \frac{\varepsilon}{\pi}\,\frac{\Xi'(\Theta)}{\Xi(\Theta)}+O(\varepsilon^2)\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow 0\). The book also shows that the remainder is in fact \(O(\varepsilon^3)\).
Source: ch/ch07.tex, label prop:mass.




Proposition 3.3.1, page 61 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(P_a(x)=a/(\pi(a^2+x^2))\) for \(a>0\) be the Poisson (Cauchy) kernel, \(P_{-a}=-P_a\), and \(P_0\) the unit point mass at the origin, and write \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\) for the total variation norm on \(\mathbb{R}\). For \(\varepsilon>0\) the Thorin density \(\rho_\varepsilon(\theta)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+i\theta)\) of the completed zeta function \(\xi\) is a sum over the zeros \(\rho=\beta+i\gamma\) with \(\gamma>0\) of kernels \(P_{1/2+\varepsilon - \beta}(\theta - \gamma)\) together with their reflections at \(-\gamma\): a zero on the line \(\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12\) with ordinate \(\gamma\) contributes \(P_\varepsilon\) centred at \(\gamma\), and a pair of off line zeros \(\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma\) with \(0<\delta<\frac12\) contributes \(P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta}\) centred at \(\gamma\). Let \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(0<\delta<\frac12\). (i) If two line zeros at height \(\gamma\) are replaced by the quadruple \(\frac12\pm\delta\pm i\gamma\), the density near \(\gamma\) changes by \(2g\), where \(g=\frac12(P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta}) - P_\varepsilon\) is the change per displaced zero, and for \(\delta<\varepsilon\), \(\|g\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4\pi}(\delta/\varepsilon)^2+O(\delta^4/\varepsilon^4)\). (ii) If the pair \(\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma\) exists but a list of line zeros omits it, the difference is \(P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta}\), and its total variation norm is \(2\) for \(\delta\le\varepsilon\) and \(\frac8\pi\arctan\sqrt{(\delta+\varepsilon)/(\delta - \varepsilon)} - 2=\frac4\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)\) for \(\delta>\varepsilon\). (iii) For \(\delta>\varepsilon\) the negative part of \(\frac12(P_{\varepsilon+\delta}+P_{\varepsilon - \delta})\), the density of one displaced zero, has mass \(\frac2\pi\arctan\sqrt{(\delta+\varepsilon)/(\delta - \varepsilon)} - \frac12=\frac1\pi\arcsin(\varepsilon/\delta)=\frac{\varepsilon}{\pi\delta}+O(\varepsilon^3/\delta^3)\). The expansion \(g=\frac{\delta^2}{2}\,\partial_a^2P_a|_{a=\varepsilon}+O(\delta^4)\) behind (i), by which the signature grows like the square of the displacement, is Proposition 19.7 of Polson (2026).
Source: ch/ch08.tex, label prop:signature.




Proposition 3.4.1, page 66 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed zeta function and, for \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(T>0\), let \(M_\varepsilon(T)=\pi^{-1}\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac12+\varepsilon+it)\,dt\) be the cumulative Thorin mass at resolution \(\varepsilon\) up to height \(T\); it equals \(\pi^{-1}\arg\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon+iT)\), with the argument continued along the vertical line from the real axis, where \(\xi>0\). Let \(T>0\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\xi\) has no zero on the segment from \(\frac12+\varepsilon\) to \(\frac12+\varepsilon+iT\), \(\pi M_\varepsilon(T)=\frac{\partial}{\partial\varepsilon}\int_0^T\log\bigl|\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon+it)\bigr|\,dt\), and for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\int_0^T\log\bigl|\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon+it)\bigr|\,dt=\int_0^T\log\bigl|\xi(\frac12+it)\bigr|\,dt+\pi\int_0^\varepsilon M_{\varepsilon'}(T)\,d\varepsilon'\), where \(M_{\varepsilon'}(T)\) is defined except for the finitely many \(\varepsilon'\) at which the segment meets a zero.
Source: ch/ch09.tex, label prop:littlewood.




Proposition 3.4.2, page 67 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed zeta function. For \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(T>0\) let \(M_\varepsilon(T)=\pi^{-1}\arg\xi(\frac12+\varepsilon+iT)\) be the cumulative Thorin mass, the argument being continued along the vertical line from the real axis, where \(\xi>0\), and let \(\tau_\varepsilon(T)\) be \(\pi^{-1}\) times the change of \(\arg\xi\) along the horizontal segment from \(\frac12+\varepsilon+iT\) to \(\frac12+iT\). Let \(N(T)\) be the number of zeros \(\rho\) with \(0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T\), and \(\nu(\sigma,T)\) the number of those with \(\operatorname{Re}\rho>\sigma\), both counted with multiplicity. Let \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(T>0\), with \(T\) not the ordinate of a zero and no zero of \(\xi\) on the segment from \(\frac12+\varepsilon\) to \(\frac12+\varepsilon+iT\). Then \(M_\varepsilon(T)+\tau_\varepsilon(T)=N(T) - 2\,\nu(\frac12+\varepsilon,T)\). The segment condition holds at \(\varepsilon=\frac12\), and \(\nu(1,T)=0\), which gives the unconditional count \(N(T)=M_{1/2}(T)+\tau_{1/2}(T)\), and \(\nu(\frac12+\varepsilon,T)=\frac12\,[N(T) - M_\varepsilon(T) - \tau_\varepsilon(T)]\) for every \(\varepsilon\) satisfying the hypotheses.
Source: ch/ch09.tex, label prop:zerodensity.







Corollary 4.1.2, page 77 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. First stated in Polson (2026), On Hilbert’s 8th Problem: the reciprocal Xi clock, Thorin measures, van Dantzig pairs, zero free approximations, hitting times and the reciprocal zeta function, first edition, Independently published.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(G(u)=\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)/\xi(\tfrac12)\), so that \(1/G\) is the reciprocal Xi function (the clock). A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on \([0,\infty)\) whose Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-bx-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+x/t)\,U(dt)\bigr)\) with drift \(b\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(U\ge0\). The Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if there are GGC random variables \(X_N\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-uX_N}\to1/G(u)\) for all \(u\) in a set with an accumulation point in \((0,\infty)\).
Source: ch/ch11.tex, label cor:weak:closure.




Corollary 4.1.3, page 80 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi(s)=\tfrac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) be the completed Riemann zeta function. A positive continuous function \(f\) on \((0,\infty)\) is hyperbolically completely monotone (HCM) if for every \(u>0\) the function \(v\mapsto f(uv)f(u/v)\) is completely monotone in \(w=v+v^{-1}\) on \([2,\infty)\). (i) For every \(\alpha\ge1\) the function \(\varphi_\alpha(u)=\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt u)\) is HCM, unconditionally. (ii) The reciprocal Xi function \(\varphi_{1/2}(u)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt u)\), the clock, is HCM if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds. Part (ii) is noted in versions 21 and 23 of Polson’s arXiv paper 1708.02653; here (i) and (ii) follow from Theorem 3.7 and Proposition 3.4 of Polson (2026) with Bondesson’s theorem.
Source: ch/ch11.tex, label cor:hcm.




Corollary 4.2.5, page 88 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), and \(\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2}\bigr)\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})\) the Pólya kernel, so that \(\Xi(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du\). For real \(t\) let \(H_t(z)=\tfrac12\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(2u)\cos(zu)\,du\), so that \(H_0(z)=\tfrac18\Xi(z/2)\), and let \(\varphi_t(s)=H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)\) for \(s>0\), so that \(\varphi_0(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\). Let \(\Lambda\) be the de Bruijn Newman constant, defined by the property that \(H_t\) has only real zeros exactly when \(t\ge\Lambda\). Then \(\varphi_t\) is HCM if and only if \(t\ge\Lambda\). Hence \(\varphi_t\) is HCM for \(t\ge0.22\) (by the bound \(\Lambda\le0.22\) of the Polymath project), \(\varphi_t\) is not HCM for \(t<0\) (by the theorem of Rodgers and Tao that \(\Lambda\ge0\)), and RH holds if and only if \(\varphi_t\) is HCM for every \(t>0\).
Source: ch/boschA.tex, label bh:cor:dbn.




Question 4.2.7, page 89 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\). Let \(W\) be the positive random variable, which exists unconditionally, with \(\mathbb{E}W^{it}=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+t)\) for real \(t\) and \(\mathbb{E}W^z=\Xi(0)/\Xi(z)\) for \(|\operatorname{Re}z|<\gamma_1\), where \(\gamma_1\approx14.1347\) is the smallest positive ordinate of a zero of \(\xi\). For which real \(\beta\) is the density of \(W^\beta\) HCM (hyperbolically completely monotone)? On the Cauchy side, for \(|C|\) with \(C\) a standard Cauchy variable, so that \(\mathbb{E}|C|^z=\sec(\pi z/2)\), the answer is \(|\beta|\ge2\) (Bosch’s theorem).
Source: ch/boschA.tex, label bh:q:beta.




Question 4.2.8, page 89 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), and let \(W\) be the positive random variable, which exists unconditionally, with \(\mathbb{E}W^z=\Xi(0)/\Xi(z)\) for \(|\operatorname{Re}z|<\gamma_1\), where \(\gamma_1\approx14.1347\) is the smallest positive ordinate of a zero of \(\xi\). Does HCM (hyperbolic complete monotonicity) of the density of \(W^\beta\) for a single real \(\beta\) imply the Riemann Hypothesis?
Source: ch/boschA.tex, label bh:q:single.




Theorem 4.3.2, page 91 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\Omega=\mathbb{C}\setminus(-\infty,0]\) and let \(h\) be a positive function on \((0,\infty)\). Call \(h\) HCM if it is continuous and for every \(u>0\) the function \(v\mapsto h(uv)h(u/v)\) is completely monotone in \(w=v+v^{-1}\) on \([2,\infty)\). Then \(h\) is HCM if and only if \(h\) continues to a zero free analytic function on \(\Omega\) and its elasticity \(\varepsilon_h(x)=-xh'(x)/h(x)\) is a Pick function, that is, \(\operatorname{Im}\varepsilon_h(x)\ge0\) for \(\operatorname{Im}x>0\).
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:thm:crit.




Theorem 4.3.6, page 94 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), and let \(\gamma\) run over the zeros of \(\Xi\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0\), counted with multiplicity. Let \(\varphi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)=\prod_\gamma(1+s/\gamma^2)^{-1}\) be the reciprocal Xi function, let \(\delta_*=\max_\gamma|\arg\gamma|\) be the largest angle of these zeros (the maximum is attained if some zero is off the critical line, and \(\delta_*=0\) if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds), and put \(\alpha_\xi=2\delta_*/\pi\) and \(p_*=1-\alpha_\xi\). Unconditionally, for real \(p\) the function \(x\mapsto\varphi(x^p)\) on \((0,\infty)\) is HCM (hyperbolically completely monotone) if and only if \(|p|\le p_*=1-\alpha_\xi\). Equivalently, \(\varphi(x^{1/\beta})\) is HCM if and only if \(|\beta|\ge1/(1-\alpha_\xi)\). The Riemann Hypothesis is the statement \(\alpha_\xi=0\), that is, \(p_*=1\).
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:thm:power.




Corollary 4.3.7, page 94 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\varphi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\) the reciprocal Xi function and \(\varepsilon_\varphi(s)=-s\varphi'(s)/\varphi(s)=\tfrac{\sqrt s}{2}\,\frac{\xi'}{\xi}\bigl(\tfrac12+\sqrt s\bigr)\) its elasticity. The following are equivalent. (i) The Riemann Hypothesis. (ii) \(\varphi\) is HCM. (iii) \(\varphi(x^p)\) is HCM for every \(|p|<1\). (iv) \(\varepsilon_\varphi\) is a Pick function (analytic on the upper half plane with nonnegative imaginary part). (v) \(\operatorname{Im}\bigl[z\,(\xi'/\xi)(\tfrac12+z)\bigr]\ge0\) for all \(z\) with \(\operatorname{Re}z>0\) and \(\operatorname{Im}z>0\).
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:cor:rh.




Corollary 4.3.8, page 95 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), \(\gamma\) the zeros of \(\Xi\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0\) counted with multiplicity, \(\varphi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\) the reciprocal Xi function with elasticity \(\varepsilon_\varphi(s)=-s\varphi'(s)/\varphi(s)\), and \(\delta_*=\max_\gamma|\arg\gamma|\). Let \(T_0=3\times10^{12}\). RH has been verified for all zeros with \(0<\operatorname{Re}\gamma\le T_0\) (Platt and Trudgian 2021). Hence \(\delta_*<\arctan(1/(2T_0))\) and \(\varphi(x^p)\) is HCM for all \(|p|\le1-\frac{1}{\pi T_0}\), where \(1-\frac{1}{\pi T_0}>1-1.1\times10^{-13}\). Unconditionally, \(\operatorname{Im}\varepsilon_\varphi(s)\ge0\) on the sector \(0<\arg s<\pi-1/T_0\).
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:cor:uncond.




Theorem 4.3.10, page 96 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), \(\gamma\) the zeros of \(\Xi\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0\) counted with multiplicity, \(\varphi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\) the reciprocal Xi function and \(\psi(s)=-\varphi'(s)/\varphi(s)=\sum_\gamma(s+\gamma^2)^{-1}\). A Stieltjes function is a function \(a/s+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\sigma(dt)/(s+t)\) with \(a,b\ge0\) and \(\sigma\ge0\) a measure satisfying \(\int(1+t)^{-1}\sigma(dt)<\infty\). Let \(T_0=3\times10^{12}\), so that every zero \(\gamma\) with \(0<\operatorname{Re}\gamma\le T_0\) is real (Platt and Trudgian 2021), and let \(\mathcal E_{T_0}=\bigl\{x+iy:\ x<-T_0^2+T_0+\tfrac14,\ y^2<\tfrac12-x\bigr\}\). Split \(\psi=S_{\mathrm{on}}+R_{\mathrm{off}}\), where \(S_{\mathrm{on}}(s)=\sum_{\gamma\ \mathrm{real}}(s+\gamma^2)^{-1}\) is the sum over the zeros on the critical line and \(R_{\mathrm{off}}\) is the same sum over the nonreal \(\gamma\). For a nonreal zero \(\gamma\) let \(D_\gamma\) be the closed disc with diameter the segment from \(-\gamma^2\) to \(-\bar\gamma^2\). Then (i) \(S_{\mathrm{on}}\) is a Stieltjes function, with measure \(\sum_{\gamma\ \mathrm{real}}\delta_{\gamma^2}\); (ii) \(R_{\mathrm{off}}\) is meromorphic on \(\mathbb{C}\) and nonnegative on \([0,\infty)\), for every nonreal \(\gamma\) the disc \(D_\gamma\), and with it the poles \(-\gamma^2\) and \(-\bar\gamma^2\) of \(R_{\mathrm{off}}\) on its boundary, lies in \(\mathcal E_{T_0}\), and \(\operatorname{Im}R_{\mathrm{off}}\le0\) at every point of the upper half plane outside these discs; (iii) \(\psi>0\) on \([0,\infty)\), and \(\operatorname{Im}\psi(s)<0\) at every \(s=x+iy\) with \(y>0\) outside \(\mathcal E_{T_0}\).
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:thm:local.




Question 4.3.12, page 99 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), \(\Phi\) the Pólya kernel (with \(\Xi(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cos(\theta u)\,du\)) and, for real \(t\), \(H_t(z)=\tfrac12\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(2u)\cos(zu)\,du\) the de Bruijn Newman deformation, so that \(H_0(z)=\tfrac18\Xi(z/2)\). Let \(\delta_*(t)\) be the largest angle \(|\arg z|\) over the zeros \(z\) of \(H_t\) with \(\operatorname{Re}z>0\) and \(p_*(t)=1-\tfrac2\pi\delta_*(t)\); whenever the zeros of \(H_t\) satisfy \(|\arg z|<\pi/4\), the function \(x\mapsto H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt{x^p})\) is HCM if and only if \(|p|\le p_*(t)\). Describe \(p_*(t)\) for \(t<0\). By Rodgers and Tao, \(p_*(t)<1\) for every \(t<0\). Assume RH; how fast does \(1-p_*(t)\to0\) as \(t\uparrow0\)?
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:q:four.




Theorem 4.3.13, page 99 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), \(\gamma\) the zeros of \(\Xi\) with \(\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0\) counted with multiplicity, \(\varphi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\) the reciprocal Xi function with elasticity \(\varepsilon_\varphi(s)=-s\varphi'(s)/\varphi(s)=\tfrac{\sqrt s}{2}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)=\sum_\gamma\frac{s}{s+\gamma^2}\), \(\delta_*=\max_\gamma|\arg\gamma|\) and \(p_*=1-2\delta_*/\pi\). A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on \([0,\infty)\) whose Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt)\bigr)\) with drift \(b\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(U\ge0\). Let \(0<p\le p_*\). Then \(\varphi(s^p)=\mathbb{E}e^{-sX_p}\) for a GGC variable \(X_p\) with no drift. If \(p<p_*\), its Thorin measure has the density \(u_p(\tau)=\frac{p}{\pi\tau}\operatorname{Im}\varepsilon_\varphi\bigl(\tau^pe^{ip\pi}\bigr)=\frac{p}{2\pi\tau}\operatorname{Im}\Bigl[z\,\frac{\xi'}{\xi}\bigl(\tfrac12+z\bigr)\Bigr]_{z=\tau^{p/2}e^{ip\pi/2}}\ge0\) for \(\tau>0\), which in terms of the zeros is \(u_p(\tau)=\frac{p}{\pi\tau}\sum_\gamma\operatorname{Im}\frac{\tau^pe^{ip\pi}}{\tau^pe^{ip\pi}+\gamma^2}\). If \(p=p_*\), its Thorin measure is \(u_{p_*}(\tau)\,d\tau\) plus a unit atom at \(|\gamma|^{2/p_*}\) for every zero \(\gamma\) with \(\arg\gamma=-\delta_*\), counted with multiplicity, that is, one atom for each conjugate pair of zeros at the extreme angle; when \(p_*=1\) there is an atom at \(\gamma^2\) for every zero, and \(u_1=0\).
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:thm:ggc.




Corollary 4.3.14, page 100 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: conditional on the Riemann Hypothesis.
Statement. Assume the Riemann Hypothesis. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function, \(\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)\), \(\gamma\) the (real, positive) zeros of \(\Xi\) counted with multiplicity, \(\varphi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\), and for \(0<p<1\) let \(X_p\) be the generalized gamma convolution (GGC) variable with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-sX_p}=\varphi(s^p)\); a GGC is a law on \([0,\infty)\) whose Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt)\bigr)\) with drift \(b\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(U\ge0\). Let \(L_p=Z_p/\tilde Z_p\) be the ratio of independent positive \(p\) stable variables, whose density \(\frac{\sin p\pi}{\pi}\,\frac{t^{p-1}}{t^{2p}+2t^p\cos p\pi+1}\) on \((0,\infty)\) is Lamperti’s; its power \(L_p^{\,p}\) is Bosch’s variable \(T_\alpha\) with \(\alpha=p\). Writing \(\mathcal L(Y)\) for the law of a random variable \(Y\), the Thorin measure of \(X_p\) is \(U_p=p\sum_\gamma\mathcal L\bigl(\gamma^{2/p}L_p\bigr)\), and \(X_p\stackrel{d}{=}S_pX^{1/p}\), where \(X=\sum_\gamma e_\gamma/\gamma^2\) is the clock variable, with independent standard exponential variables \(e_\gamma\), and \(S_p\) is a positive \(p\) stable variable independent of \(X\) with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-\lambda S_p}=e^{-\lambda^p}\). At \(p=\tfrac12\), \(L_{1/2}\stackrel{d}{=}C^2\) for a standard Cauchy variable \(C\), and \(U_{1/2}=\tfrac12\sum_\gamma\mathcal L(\gamma^4C^2)\). As \(p\uparrow1\), \(L_p\to1\) and \(U_p\to\sum_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}\) vaguely, the Thorin measure of \(\varphi\) itself.
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:cor:lamperti.




Corollary 4.3.15, page 101 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: proved.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and \(\varphi(s)=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)\) the reciprocal Xi function. A generalized gamma convolution (GGC) is a law on \([0,\infty)\) whose Laplace transform is \(\exp\bigl(-bs-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+s/t)\,U(dt)\bigr)\) with drift \(b\ge0\) and Thorin measure \(U\ge0\). For \(0<p<1\) say that \(X_p\) exists if \(\varphi(s^p)=\mathbb{E}e^{-sX_p}\) for a GGC random variable \(X_p\). Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if \(X_p\) exists for every \(p\in(0,1)\). Unconditionally, using the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis to height \(T_0=3\times10^{12}\) (Platt and Trudgian 2021), \(X_p\) exists for \(0<p\le1-1/(\pi T_0)\), in particular for \(0<p\le1-1.1\times10^{-13}\), and its Thorin measure then has the density \(u_p(\tau)=\frac{p}{2\pi\tau}\operatorname{Im}\Bigl[z\,\frac{\xi'}{\xi}\bigl(\tfrac12+z\bigr)\Bigr]_{z=\tau^{p/2}e^{ip\pi/2}}\) for \(\tau>0\).
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:cor:rhX.




Question 4.3.16, page 101 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function and, for \(0<p<1\), let \(X_p\) be the variable with \(\mathbb{E}e^{-sX_p}=\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+s^{p/2})\), a generalized gamma convolution whenever it exists; unconditionally it exists for \(0<p\le1-1.1\times10^{-13}\), and RH holds if and only if it exists for every \(p\in(0,1)\). In particular \(X_{1/2}\) has Laplace transform \(\xi(\tfrac12)/\xi(\tfrac12+s^{1/4})\) and exists without any hypothesis. Construct \(X_{1/2}\) from Brownian motion, Bessel processes or the Biane, Pitman and Yor variables without reference to the zeros. A construction that survived \(p\uparrow1\) would prove RH.
Source: ch/boschB.tex, label bs:q:five.




Question 4.3.17, page 102 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times, edition 1. New in this book.
Status: open.
Statement. Let \(\xi\) be the completed Riemann zeta function.
